summary:
Working on the dashboard summary now.

I've been rebuilding the image pipeline for Keikochō, a Japanese-learning app I write for myself. The original art was all young anime-style women, which felt off for a middle-aged guy learning hiragana, so I moved everything to a colored manga style with a diverse cast. The interesting failures were on the AI casting side: without an "elderly" tag anchoring the generation, the model defaults to moe teenagers no matter what other words you throw at it, and a raised hand near someone's chest kept opening their shirt because a pose can carry the same trope as a prop. I also learned the hard way that a full-width thumbnail with a fixed pixel height crops harder as the screen gets wider — so a card that looked fine on my desktop was cutting off people's heads on my phone, because a mobile grid column is actually the *widest* case, not the narrowest.

I've also been working through Keikochō's conversation engine, which teaches by composing dialogue from grammar rules rather than generating it. When I asked for the bot to feel less like a checklist of "do you like X" questions, the fix wasn't to bolt on an LLM — a model can only pick among the reply options that exist, so if the only replies are three ways to grunt, an LLM just picks a better-timed grunt. The real fix was authoring an actual reaction: giving the bot an opinion that responds to what you specifically said, using the grammar rules the engine already had. That, plus adding cast voices, so the app's 14 characters don't all sound like the same one narrator.

On the infrastructure side, I chased a hard-to-reproduce audio bug on a home GPU box: one service auto-sized its VRAM usage at boot and another loaded lazily on first use, so who won the available memory was a coin flip that depended on boot order — the same config could pass or fail a health check depending on which service started first. Pinning the allocation instead of leaving it on "auto" fixed it for good, which was a good reminder that a green health check taken once is one sample, not proof.

highlights.oneLiner: Fixed a boot-order VRAM race with a co-located service by pinning GPU allocation instead of auto-sizing.
